title: Polymer clay sculpted sea turtle
subtitle: A miniature sea turtle figure about 8 cm long, baked in a domestic oven
excerpt: A sea turtle figure in polymer clay is built from a shaped body piece, four flat flipper pieces, and a head, joined before baking. The shell pattern is scored with a needle after assembly. Bakes at 130°C for 30 minutes. Decorative, not food-safe.
sourceNotes: Technique derived from first principles for polymer clay sculpture.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling clay that cures hard in a domestic oven at 110-130°C; decorative only, not food-safe
Warming and kneading polymer clay by hand until soft and pliable before sculpting

content.text: A sea turtle figure in
polymer clay

is an assembly of five pieces: a dome body, two front flippers, two rear flippers, and a small head. Each piece is shaped separately, joined in the raw state, then baked together. The scored shell pattern sets the look before baking. Finished figure is 8-9 cm nose to tail.

materials.name: Polymer clay, tan or sand (optional for belly)

content.text: Conditioning the clay
Conditioning

polymer clay properly prevents cracking after baking. Work 60 g of green polymer clay between your palms for two to three minutes until the clay is warm and flows without resistance. It should stretch without tearing when pulled gently. Cold, unworked clay breaks rather than bends.
Shaping the body
Roll 35 g of conditioned clay into a smooth oval: flat on the bottom, domed on top, 6 cm long, 5 cm wide, and 2 cm tall.
If adding a contrasting belly, press a flattened oval of tan clay onto the base of the body and blend the edge seam with a wooden rib. The belly should cover the flat underside only.
Shaping the flippers and head
Front flippers: roll 5 g per flipper into a teardrop shape, then flatten to 4 mm thick. Elongate to 4 cm at the longest point. Curl the tip slightly upward.
Rear flippers: roll 3 g per flipper into a shorter teardrop, 3 cm long, flattened to 3 mm. These angle downward rather than forward.
Head: roll 5 g into a rounded oval, 2 cm long. Press gently to flatten the underside. Mark two small eye indentations with a needle tool.
Assembling
Press each piece firmly against the body at the attachment point. Polymer clay bonds to itself in the raw state through pressure alone , no slip needed. Blend the seam of each join with a wooden rib.
Place the front flippers so they angle slightly forward and upward from the front quarter of the body, one on each side.
Place the rear flippers at the back quarter, angling backward and slightly downward.
Press the head to the front of the body. Blend the neck join with a wooden rib so the head sits naturally on the body without a visible gap.
Scoring the shell pattern

Use a needle tool to score the carapace pattern on the dome of the body. A sea turtle shell has a central row of five large scutes bordered by a row of smaller scutes on each side. Press lightly with the needle , 1 mm deep lines are enough. Do not cut all the way through. The pattern only needs to suggest the divisions, not be perfectly geometric.
Baking

Place the figure on a piece of baking parchment on a small oven tray. Bake at 130°C (conventional, not fan) for 30 minutes. Allow to cool fully in the oven with the door slightly open before touching. Polymer clay is flexible when hot and sets firm on cooling.
Finishing

Once cool, apply an acrylic varnish to seal and protect the surface. Matte varnish gives a natural look; satin adds a slight sheen. Polymer clay is not food-safe. Do not use the figure in a dishwasher or microwave.
Variations
Add a small loop of wire to the back before baking to turn the figure into an ornament or keyring.
Blend two greens , dark and light , for a mottled carapace colour. Marble the colours without fully mixing to keep distinct streaks.
Make a family of three turtles: 8 cm, 5 cm, and 3 cm, using the same method with proportionally smaller pieces.
Troubleshooter

items.cause: The join was not pressed firmly enough before baking, leaving an air gap
items.fix: Sand the break area with fine sandpaper. Apply liquid polymer clay as adhesive, press the pieces together, and bake for 15 more minutes at 130 degrees C.

items.cause: The clay was not conditioned fully before shaping; cold clay contains trapped stress
items.fix: Condition more thoroughly next time. Small cracks can be filled with a tiny amount of raw polymer clay, smoothed in, and re-baked for 15 minutes

items.problem: Figure collapsed or distorted in the oven
items.cause: Baking temperature too high, or the figure was not supported properly on the parchment
items.fix: Use a thermometer to verify oven temperature. For taller or top-heavy figures, prop gently with a small wad of aluminium foil while baking
